corrections.new:
Every signed request is built through one seam, and it refuses locally what a verifier would
refuse remotely: a request carrying no artifact binding does not sign, and a structurally
invalid binding cannot be built to be signed (its construction refuses it). A valid binding
still signs, so the refusal is not vacuous.

The caller's own `params._meta` survives signing unchanged, and the MCP-RE evidence block
lands at the body root rather than inside the caller's content.

A signed NOTIFICATION carries no `id` key at all — absent, never present-and-null — while
carrying the ordinary RFC 9421 evidence, and a continuation declared on one is refused. Both
custody classes emit identical notification bytes.

A presented decision mints its binding over the exact bytes presented; a caller presenting
none authors a block without one, rather than an empty or placeholder binding.

corrections.reason: this theorem's own claim, field statement. Moved from refusal at sign time to unconstructibility (Ruling 12 item 12, commit afe1cacb). 'A request carrying no artifact binding does not sign' is kept; 'a structurally invalid binding does not sign' becomes 'cannot be built to be signed', because ArtifactBinding owns the structural invariant through a private representation. The valid-binding-still-signs conjunct is kept. This is the same property at a stronger point of the type.
